title: Trim Terraform module surface area and introduce provider transition shim for networking
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Over time our networking Terraform surface has grown organically: multiple tiny modules expose many inputs, rely on implicit provider inheritance, and contain provider version constraints scattered across overlays. This increases cognitive load, causes drift during provider upgrades, and makes cross-region resource lifecycles unreliable.

Goal: Reduce the public surface of networking modules to a small stable core, remove implicit provider dependencies, and introduce a provider transition shim that centralizes provider version pinning and aliasing. Deliver a reversible rollout path with a state migration harness and CI plan-guards to ensure safe upgrades across workspaces.

What we will change:
- Collapse low-value wrapper modules (networking/shared-routes, networking/legacy-eips, networking/subnet-utils) into a single networking-core module with a narrow input surface and well-documented outputs.
- Remove implicit provider usage from modules; require provider aliasing explicitly where cross-region or cross-account resources are needed.
- Add a new infra/provider-shim module that: pins provider versions, exposes provider aliases for regions/accounts, and offers a feature-flag toggle to enable the legacy implicit-provider compatibility layer for staged migration.
- Replace "count" usage in stateful resources with for_each keyed by deterministic IDs to improve idempotency when reordering resources.
- Add Terraform plan-guard CI job that fails on diffs that touch critical networking resources without an approved migration note.
- Ship small migration helper scripts (state-mv/state-import templates) and a runbook documenting per-workspace steps for state adjustments.

Acceptance criteria:
- New networking-core module published and consumed by staging workspaces without functional regressions.
- provider-shim module with example usage in infra/README and one complete migration PR merged (#1723).
- CI plan-guard enabled in 3 canary workspaces and configured to block on critical resource diffs.
- Runbook tested and validated in staging; no more than 2 hours total downtime for a canary migration (expected zero).

Risk & mitigation:
- State manipulation errors: require a pre-migration state snapshot, automated validation steps, and a mandatory code owner approval on migration PRs.
- Provider behavior differences after pinning: run canary in us-west-2, eu-west-1 and compare plan outputs and metrics for 48 hours.
- Unexpected cost/throughput changes for NAT/EIP lifecycles: monitor networking-dashboard and throttle migrations if anomalies detected.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge provider-shim and networking-core into a feature branch; add example usage to a staging workspace.
2) Run automated migration scripts in staging and validate plans; fix any drift.
3) Enable plan-guard CI for 3 canary workspaces (staging, preprod, a small prod set).
4) Gradual wave rollout across production workspaces (10% -> 25% -> 100%).
5) Post-rollout audit: compare tag propagation, route tables and NAT metrics; close the ticket when all waves green.

Dependencies:
- ENG-582901 (terraform provider init rework) — coordination needed to avoid provider-init clashes.
- PM-44120 (release calendar) — need scheduled maintenance windows for state migrations.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Terraform+Provider+Transition+Design
- Migration runbook draft (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3-provider-shim-runbook
- GitHub PR (feature branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1723

Notes: This is intentionally conservative: we are not changing resource schemas beyond the minimal required to move from implicit to explicit providers. The provider-shim has a compatibility toggle to allow a staged removal of legacy patterns.
